source: The engine's original heuristic set (engine/ontology/heuristics.json before issue #128)

heuristics.name: Goldilocks
heuristics.description: Test too small, just right, and too big values for any bounded field.
heuristics.apply: For each field with a size or range, send one value well under it, one inside it and one well over it.

heuristics.name: Boundary edges
heuristics.description: Test values exactly at, one below, and one above a documented limit.
heuristics.apply: Find a stated limit, then send the limit itself and its two nearest neighbours.

heuristics.name: Zero and negative
heuristics.description: Test zero and negative values for any field assumed to be a positive quantity.
heuristics.apply: Send 0, -1 and a large negative number where a count, amount or size is expected.

heuristics.name: Alphabet soup
heuristics.description: Feed unicode, emoji, whitespace-only, and mixed-script strings into text fields.
heuristics.apply: Enter accented letters, a right-to-left script, emoji and only spaces, then check what is stored and shown.

heuristics.name: Monetary precision
heuristics.description: Check that monetary values never show float rounding artifacts and use consistent decimal precision.
heuristics.apply: Look at every shown or returned price and total for values like 0.30000000000000004 or mixed decimal places.

heuristics.name: Empty and null
heuristics.description: Submit empty string, null, and missing-field variants for every required field.
heuristics.apply: Leave each required field empty, send it as null, and leave it out, one field at a time.

heuristics.name: Duplicate replay
heuristics.description: Repeat an identical request/transaction and check for idempotency or unintended duplication.
heuristics.apply: Send the same order, payment or create action twice in a row and count what was created or charged.

heuristics.name: Ordering race
heuristics.description: Fire near-simultaneous or out-of-order requests against the same resource/account.
heuristics.apply: Send two changes to the same thing at the same moment, or in the reverse of the usual order.

heuristics.name: Sensitive data exposure
heuristics.description: Check that sensitive fields (secrets, PANs, tokens) are never echoed back in responses or logs.
heuristics.apply: After handling a secret, card number or token, look for it in responses, pages, errors and logs.

heuristics.name: Self-consistency
heuristics.description: Compare two responses that should logically agree (e.g. same query, different path) for contradictions.
heuristics.apply: Get the same fact two ways, such as a total and its line items, and check they agree.
